headline: Ecuadorian player banned eight years for hitting an assistant referee with a stone
facts: On 17 October, in stoppage time of a third-tier Ecuador match against Rio Aguarico, midfielder Perlaza threw a stone from the bench and hit assistant referee Ojeda in the face.
The assistant referee suffered a fractured cheekbone, needed surgery and was unable to work for 60 days; the match was stopped.

The Ecuadorian federation banned Perlaza for eight years (to 19 October 2034) and will ask FIFA to extend the ban worldwide; the club was fined USD 2,000, must repay medical costs and play three home games at a neutral venue.
background: Assaults on referees are among the most severely punished offences in football; this one came in Ecuador's third tier, far from the big leagues.
footage_terms: Ciudad de Yantzaza Rio Aguarico partido suspendido

headline: Napoli coach Allegri sent off in 3-3 draw with Roma and banned for two matches
facts: After Roma's late equaliser by Balerdi in a 3-3 draw, Allegri was shown a straight red card; he argued the goal should have been disallowed for a foul on Sam Beukema in the build-up.
Lega Serie A banned him for two matches (Monza away and Juventus away) and fined him 10,000 euros for remarks to officials and an aggressive attitude toward a Roma staff member.
Napoli first said they would appeal, but Allegri then chose not to, joked the ban could grow to four matches, and said he wanted to focus on Napoli's poor Serie A run.
background: Allegri is a veteran Italian coach with two spells at Juventus, so the ban also keeps him off the bench at his former club.
footage_terms: Allegri sent off reaction press conference

headline: Maignan sent off for shoving Tyler Adams as Bournemouth rout Milan 3-0 in Europa League
facts: Milan keeper Maignan got a straight red in the 27th minute for pushing Tyler Adams in the face during a corner; Tavernier scored the resulting penalty (Kluivert had scored an earlier penalty for handball).
Bournemouth won 3-0 and are three wins from three in the Europa League, the first English club since 1973 to win their first three games in a major European competition.
It was Ruben Amorim's first competitive game back in England since Manchester United sacked him in January; Milan later condemned racist abuse of Maignan on social media after the match.
background: Maignan has spoken out against racism before: in January 2024 he walked off at Udinese after racist chants from fans.
footage_terms: Amorim press conference after Bournemouth Milan

headline: Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton sent off for second yellow in 1-1 Europa League draw with Hoffenheim
facts: Wharton was booked for an aerial challenge before the hour and sent off in the 77th minute for a second yellow after a coming-together with Wouter Burger.
Several Palace players protested, but the referee did not change the decision and Palace played the rest of the game with ten men.
Hoffenheim led through Alexander Prass in the 7th minute; Daichi Kamada equalised for Palace in the 91st minute.
background: Wharton is an England midfielder who has been central to Palace's midfield; Palace lifted the FA Cup in 2025.

headline: Oldham manager Micky Mellon sent off for pushing his head at Sheffield Wednesday player, then Oldham win FA Cup tie
facts: Mellon was sent off in the 84th minute after he pushed his head toward Wednesday midfielder Callum Slattery during a touchline scuffle; the ESPN headline calls it a headbutt, the report body describes a push.
Slattery was booked; Oldham, from League Two, beat League One Sheffield Wednesday 2-1 after extra time with a 110th-minute winner from Will Sutton.
It was Dave Challinor's first match in charge of Sheffield Wednesday. The report mentions no FA charge. Date is the article date; match date not stated.
background: Oldham were founder members of the Premier League in 1992 and now play in League Two.

Oldham 2-1 Sheffield Wednesday FA Cup highlights

headline: FA Cup qualifier replayed after referee error with a penalty, and the same team wins again
facts: In an FA Cup second qualifying round tie, Woodford were awarded a penalty but players entered the box early; the referee gave Mulbarton an indirect free kick instead of ordering a retake.
An FA subcommittee under the Professional Game Board ordered a replay after Woodford appealed the original 2-1 Mulbarton win.
Mulbarton won the replay 2-0, both goals from Ashley Jarvis, and moved on to face Gloucester Town in the third qualifying round.
background: Both clubs play at the deep non-league level, where an FA Cup qualifying run is the biggest stage of the season.
footage_terms: Mulbarton Wanderers Woodford Town FA Cup replay
FA Cup qualifying penalty retake referee error

headline: Aaron Ramsey's Oxford play with nine, briefly eight men at Mansfield and argue over disputed red and dive card
facts: Oxford drew 1-1 at Mansfield after Luka Lynch scored on his first start; Michael Smith equalised in the 82nd minute.
Gatlin O'Donkor got a second booking with six minutes left, and Oxford were briefly down to eight when Brodie Spencer went off after an injury stoppage.

Ramsey disagreed with the first red card, arguing there was contact in the area that should have been a penalty, and disputed Peter Kioso's 75th-minute booking for diving; Kioso was later sent off for a second yellow.
background: Ramsey is a former Arsenal, Juventus and Wales midfielder who is now managing Oxford United.
footage_terms: Aaron Ramsey press conference Oxford eight men

headline: Premier League adopts World Cup time-wasting limits and some VAR checks, rejects the mouth-covering red card
facts: For 2026-27 players treated on the pitch must leave for at least one minute, throw-ins and goal kicks get a five-second countdown, and substituted players have 10 seconds to leave.
VAR can now review a second yellow card given in error and card mistaken identity within the same incident, factual errors only.
The Premier League did not adopt VAR checks on wrongly awarded corners, red cards for covering the mouth, or mandatory hydration breaks.
background: Many of these measures were approved by IFAB after trials, and several were first used at the 2026 World Cup.
footage_terms: five second countdown throw-in goal kick

headline: Neymar sent off under the Vinicius Junior rule for covering his mouth, then banned
facts: In Santos' 1-0 win over Bahia in the Brazilian Serie A, Neymar covered his mouth while arguing with Rodrigo Nestor, who alerted the referee, and Neymar was sent off.
Neymar admitted covering his mouth was wrong but denied saying anything offensive, called Nestor's move a dirty trick and said he would get back at him; Bahia condemned his alleged verbal abuse.
Brazil's sports tribunal banned him for three matches in total (one for yellow cards and two for the mouth-covering), and he is not expected back until late November.
background: The red card for covering the mouth followed Vinicius Junior's claim of racist abuse by Benfica's Gianluca Prestianni, who received a six-game ban; Neymar is Brazil's all-time leading scorer.
footage_terms: Neymar reaction red card covering mouth

headline: Panel rules Arsenal were wrongly denied a penalty against Hull after VAR review
facts: In Arsenal's 1-0 win over Hull on 7 November, Nobel Mendy held Kai Havertz, who was in an offside position; referee Farai Hallam gave no penalty and VAR Michael Oliver sent him to the monitor but the decision stood.
The five-member Key Match Incidents panel ruled unanimously that a penalty should have been awarded, because the holding came before any offside offence.
The panel reviewed 223 incidents in the first 10 rounds and found 85 percent of on-field decisions correct, rising to 97 percent after VAR.
background: Arsenal also lead the Premier League in offsides this season, with Havertz himself flagged 15 times, more than any other top-flight player.
footage_terms: Key Match Incidents Arsenal Hull penalty

headline: River Plate's Montiel sent off in the Superclasico; ban cut from three to two matches on appeal
facts: Montiel was sent off in the second half of the Superclasico, which River lost; referee Nicolas Ramirez reported a foul on Lautaro Blanco as serious foul play.
The AFA disciplinary tribunal first gave three matches, then cut it to two after appeal; he missed the win over Aldosivi and will miss the Clausura round-of-16 tie against Lanus.
River felt the punishment was excessive and pointed out that Blanco was not sent off for a similar foul on Tobias Andrada.
background: The River-Boca Superclasico is Argentina's biggest fixture, and Montiel is a World Cup winner with Argentina in 2022.

headline: Head of Turkish football refereeing detained in probe over how referees are appointed and scored
facts: On 29 September Turkish authorities detained the head of the national refereeing body, his deputy and five others, seven people in total.
Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said the probe concerns alleged irregularities in how referees are classified, assigned, scored and appointed, and in rule exams.
It is not yet clear whether the arrests link to earlier cases: the federation suspended 149 referees over a betting scandal last year and 17 club officials were detained in July.
background: Turkish football has been rocked by betting and match-fixing investigations in recent years, and Super Lig refereeing is a regular flashpoint for clubs like Besiktas.
footage_terms: Super Lig referees betting scandal explained

headline: Arsenal appeal 16-year-old Max Dowman's red card in Carabao Cup shootout loss to Fleetwood
facts: Fourth-tier Fleetwood beat Arsenal on penalties after a 1-1 draw; Loupalo-Bi scored in the 21st minute and Viktor Gyokeres equalised.
Dowman, 16, was shown a red card in the 85th minute for kicking out at Harrison Neal after a rough tackle.
Arsenal planned to appeal, with paperwork due to the FA by Thursday, hoping for a ruling before the Premier League game at Liverpool on Sunday; Arteta was tight-lipped about his reaction.
background: Dowman is a teenage Arsenal academy talent, and the Carabao Cup exit to a fourth-tier side was a major upset.
footage_terms: Arteta Dowman red card press conference

headline: Ronaldo's 'goal' for Al Nassr: league credits him, Opta says own goal
facts: In Al Nassr's 3-1 win over Al Faisaly, Ronaldo headed Joao Felix's free kick and the ball was deflected in by defender Andrei Girotto.
The Saudi Pro League credited Ronaldo, while stats provider Opta ruled it an own goal.
With the goal, Ronaldo's official career total is 985; without it, 984. He also scored a hat trick in a 5-3 win over Al Kholood later that week.
background: Ronaldo has played in Saudi Arabia for Al Nassr since leaving Manchester United and joining the club in early 2023.
footage_terms: Ronaldo goal Al Faisaly own goal debate

headline: Luton boss Wilshere sent off for reaction to referee after no foul before Stevenage's opener
facts: Stevenage beat Luton 2-1; Luton's bench was angry that Dan Phillips was not penalised for a foul on Liam Walsh in the build-up to Dan Kemp's 23rd-minute opener.
Wilshere's reaction to referee Andrew Humphries was judged unacceptable and he watched the rest from the dressing room.
Assistant boss Chris Powell said officials should have handled the incidents better and that he believed Josh Magennis's winner came from an offside position.
background: Wilshere, a former Arsenal and England midfielder, is in his early days as a manager; he was also later involved in a post-match scuffle with Barnsley's boss in October.

headline: IFAB panels reject five-second countdown for corners and free kicks, back single coin toss for shootouts, announce full VAR review
facts: The football and technical advisory panels did not back extending the five-second countdown to corner kicks and free kicks, citing tactical complexity.

They supported a single coin toss for penalty shootouts, where the winning captain picks the goal or shooting first or second, and heard that the goalkeeper injury-delay trial has shown very positive initial results.
IFAB announced a comprehensive VAR review using stakeholder feedback and independent data; input feeds the Annual Business Meeting in Zurich on 14 January 2027.
background: IFAB, the body that writes the Laws of the Game, has been pushing a faster tempo after the time-wasting measures introduced for 2026/27.

headline: UEFA referee chief Rosetti explains faster restarts, new VAR areas and the Clear Line video library
facts: Referees will be strict on time-wasting: substituted players have 10 seconds to leave, treated players leave for a minute, and delayed throw-ins or goal kicks can cost a corner after a five-second countdown.

VAR can now correct a sanction given to the wrong player and cancel a clearly wrong second yellow; UEFA chose not to adopt the mouth-covering red card and leaving the field in protest as red-card offences.
UEFA's Clear Line library has over 100 videos showing when VAR should and should not intervene, and referee numbers across Europe have grown by 90,000 since the Be a Referee campaign began in 2023.
background: Rosetti, a former top referee, has run UEFA refereeing since 2010 and has pushed the idea of minimal VAR interference.
footage_terms: Rosetti UEFA referees briefing Champions League

headline: UEFA tells referee chiefs VAR is for clear and obvious errors only, not to re-referee matches
facts: UEFA's refereeing chief chaired a meeting of referee heads from all 55 member associations and stated that VAR should step in only for clear and obvious errors.
Delegates unanimously backed faster restarts; UEFA does not plan to adopt other optional World Cup measures such as red cards for covering the mouth or VAR checks on corners.
UEFA cited the World Cup incident where Switzerland's Breel Embolo was sent off for a second yellow against Argentina after a caution for Leandro Paredes was overturned on review.
background: This is the background statement before the 2026/27 season; the mistaken-identity check was one of the newly approved VAR areas.
footage_terms: Embolo second yellow Argentina Switzerland World Cup
UEFA VAR clear and obvious error
World Cup 2026 VAR controversy Paredes yellow

headline: IFAB approves time-wasting countdowns, substitution limits and new VAR areas in February package
facts: After its AGM in Wales, IFAB introduced a five-second visual countdown for delayed throw-ins and goal kicks, a 10-second exit for substituted players and a one-minute wait off the pitch after treatment.
VAR may intervene on a clearly wrong second yellow, mistaken identity and, as an option, a clearly wrongly awarded corner.
The 2026/27 Laws take effect on 1 July 2026 and include referee body cameras as a competition option and a new dropped-ball rule.
background: This package set up the rules that leagues, including the Premier League and UEFA, have now been applying this season.
footage_terms: five second countdown goal kick explained

headline: IFAB unanimously approves red card for covering the mouth in confrontations and for walking off in protest
facts: After a special meeting in Vancouver, IFAB unanimously approved two FIFA-proposed amendments, both at the competition organiser's discretion.

A player who covers his mouth during a confrontation may be shown a red card, and a player who leaves the field in protest of a referee decision may be sent off; a team that causes abandonment will in principle forfeit.
The measures were to be implemented at the 2026 World Cup, with the 48 teams informed in the following weeks.
background: The mouth-covering rule followed the Vinicius Junior and Prestianni controversy at a Champions League tie and is the rule Neymar fell foul of this autumn.
footage_terms: IFAB mouth covering red card rule
football rule change covering mouth explained

headline: IFAB clarifies VAR protocol for attacking-team offences before the ball is in play
facts: VAR may recommend an on-field review for clear attacking-team offences before a corner or free kick is taken if the offence directly affects a goal, penalty or disciplinary sanction.
If the referee confirms the offence, the right sanction is applied and the corner or free kick is retaken.
It was approved for the 2026 World Cup and will be reviewed after the tournament before any wider use.
background: The clarification is related to disputes over players pushing or blocking at set pieces, a recurring complaint about VAR.
footage_terms: IFAB VAR protocol set piece offence
goal disallowed foul before corner VAR

headline: Besiktas blast referee and VAR after Trossard slapped in the face with no punishment
facts: In Besiktas' 1-0 loss to Alanyaspor, Fidan Aliti slapped Leandro Trossard in the face off the ball; the referee and VAR took no action.
Trossard, playing only his second Super Lig game after leaving Arsenal, said it should have been a straight red.
Besiktas called the refereeing a disgrace, said they do not want referee Kayatepe and VAR Birincioglu in their matches again and vowed to pursue the matter.
background: The incident came weeks before Turkey's refereeing chief was detained in a separate government probe into referee appointments.

headline: Australian top referees strike ends as Football Australia reaches deal after a month
facts: Nearly 100 top referees, represented by the PFRA, had been on strike since 4 September over a Football Australia plan to contract them to the APL rather than to FA.
The strike threatened the Australia Cup final and the start of the A-League seasons, including the opening Sydney derby on 16 October.
The 2 October deal keeps referees employed by Football Australia for 2026-27, with the APL covering the costs of A-League matches while longer-term talks continue.
background: Referees rarely strike in top-level football, which is why the threat of bringing in overseas officials made headlines.
footage_terms: Australia Cup final 2026 South Melbourne Victory

headline: VAR lets Man United's injury-time equaliser stand in 4-4 draw with Aston Villa as pundits argue over a foul on the keeper
facts: Patrick Dorgu scored Manchester United's injury-time equaliser from a corner in a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, while Villa keeper Zion Suzuki felt Senne Lammens had fouled him.
Referee Chris Kavanagh and VAR Craig Pawson left the goal standing; ESPN's Andy Davies called it correct but borderline, while United fan Mark Goldbridge argued VAR should have intervened.
The article dates the match 8 November; ESPN's coverage the same week shows Mauricio Pochettino has just taken over as United head coach.
background: Manchester United have been through several managers since Sir Alex Ferguson left in 2013, and Mauricio Pochettino is the latest to take the job.

headline: VAR review sends Lisandro Martinez off as Chelsea beat Man United 2-0
facts: Chelsea beat Manchester United 2-0 on 31 October; referee Peter Bankes initially gave no penalty or card for Martinez's aerial challenge on Wesley Fofana.
After a VAR review by James Bell, Bankes awarded Chelsea a penalty and sent Martinez off for a second yellow, in the 61st minute.
ESPN's Andy Davies judged the VAR intervention correct, saying Martinez led with his arm and caught Fofana's head.
background: Martinez, who won the 2022 World Cup with Argentina, has a reputation for aggressive aerial and defensive challenges.
footage_terms: Lisandro Martinez red card Chelsea Man United

headline: No red for Bogle after studs-up Achilles challenge on Tel in Leeds' win over Spurs; Tottenham write to Pro Ref
facts: Leeds won 1-0 at Elland Road; Jayden Bogle caught Mathys Tel on the Achilles with his studs, and Tel was replaced after treatment.
Referee John Brooks gave no card, and after a lengthy VAR review no serious foul play was found; Tottenham plan to write to Pro Ref to ask why no red card was shown.
Bogle was then reportedly subjected to racist abuse on social media; Leeds and Tottenham both condemned it and the Premier League warned of bans and prosecution.
background: Leeds and Tottenham met in the Premier League this season, and Tottenham said they would take the VAR decision up with the referees' body.
footage_terms: Bogle Tel challenge VAR Leeds Tottenham
Tottenham Pro Ref letter Bogle red card

headline: Arteta calls Sunderland penalty for Konsa foul 'unacceptable' as Arsenal still win 2-0
facts: Early in the second half Sunderland were given a penalty when Ezri Konsa was judged to have fouled Dan Ballard at a corner; referee Stuart Attwell gave it and VAR upheld it.
Arteta called it unacceptable at this level, compared the contact to a judo throw and warned it could affect Arsenal's title chances.
David Raya saved Enzo Le Fee's penalty, Bruno Guimaraes scored from outside the box and Bukayo Saka added an injury-time penalty in a 2-0 Arsenal win.
background: Arteta has a history of public complaints about officials, and Arsenal were Premier League champions last season.
footage_terms: Raya saves penalty Le Fee Arsenal Sunderland

headline: VAR error in Liverpool v Arsenal? No penalty for Timber pulling Isak's shirt
facts: In the 34th minute of Liverpool v Arsenal, Alexander Isak appeared to have his shirt pulled by Jurrien Timber as he went to head a cross.
Referee Andy Madley played on and VAR Stuart Attwell cleared the no-penalty decision.

ESPN's Andy Davies called the non-intervention an error by VAR, arguing Timber made no attempt to play the ball. The article gives no date; 1 November is inferred from a report that Arsenal were due at Liverpool that Sunday.
background: Isak joined Liverpool from Newcastle in 2025 in a record British transfer.
footage_terms: Isak Timber shirt pull Liverpool Arsenal
Liverpool Arsenal VAR penalty claim Isak

headline: Haaland's stoppage-time VAR-awarded penalty sends Norway past Denmark into Nations League quarter-finals
facts: Norway beat Denmark 3-2 after Denmark led 2-0 inside 15 minutes; Odegaard equalised in the 87th minute.
VAR reviewed a handball by Denmark's Joachim Andersen in stoppage time and Norway were awarded a penalty, which Haaland scored at 95:45.
Haaland was booked for excessive celebration after tearing off his shirt; he now has 68 international goals in 61 appearances and 25 Nations League goals, a record.
background: Haaland is Norway's all-time leading scorer, and the win secured a Nations League quarter-final place for Norway, to be played in March.
footage_terms: Haaland penalty Norway Denmark Nations League
